"""The instruments Manual LIVE may trade, and the one rule that decides membership.

This module is the whitelist and nothing else. It holds no account state, makes no request and
imports nothing at all, so every layer that has to judge a symbol - the LIVE config, the
adapter registry, the routes, the order router, the PAPER runtime, the chart history - can ask
the same question of the same answer rather than each keeping its own tuple.

It sits at the crypto package root rather than inside `live/` on purpose. `live/` is the only
package allowed to touch a real Binance account, and a structural test asserts that nothing
outside it imports from it - the PAPER terminal must not be able to reach the account code even
transitively. The whitelist is needed on both sides of that line, so it belongs on neither: it
is a fact about which instruments this build is about, not about any account.

Why a whitelist rather than "whatever Binance lists": every symbol added here costs real reads
(filters, commission, bracket table, book) and a real screen that has to be correct about
quantity precision and minimum notional. Binance lists hundreds of perpetuals. Three were asked
for, three are supported, and a fourth is a decision somebody makes on purpose by editing this
tuple - not something a query parameter can do.

`DEFAULT_SYMBOL` is first in the tuple on purpose: it is what every route answers when the
caller names nothing, and it is BTCUSDT because that is the instrument the existing audit
mirror, performance cursor and paper ledger are about. A deployment that defaulted elsewhere
would silently re-point those files.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

#: Ordered. The screen's tabs read left to right in this order, and `DEFAULT_SYMBOL` is the
#: first entry rather than a second constant that could drift from it.
SUPPORTED_SYMBOLS: tuple[str, ...] = ("BTCUSDT", "ETHUSDT", "SOLUSDT")

DEFAULT_SYMBOL = SUPPORTED_SYMBOLS[0]

#: Reject code, carried to the API so a refusal reads the same wherever it was raised.
SYMBOL_NOT_SUPPORTED = "SYMBOL_NOT_SUPPORTED"

#: Symbols admitted at runtime: the current HOT symbol, and nothing else.
#:
#: The whitelist above stays the policy for the instruments this build is *about*. Dynamic HOT
#: Trading adds exactly one more: whichever USDT perpetual the HOT scan selected, admitted by
#: the HOT service only after Binance's own `exchangeInfo` said PERPETUAL, TRADING, USDT, and
#: retired when the HOT slot moves on. A query parameter still cannot admit anything; only
#: `admit_dynamic` can, and only the HOT service calls it.
_dynamic: set[str] = set()


def _shape_ok(symbol: str) -> bool:
    """A conservative shape check on top of the exchange's word: USDT-quoted, no separators or
    whitespace, bounded length. Binance names some perpetuals in Chinese characters, so letters
    are not limited to ASCII."""
    return (4 < len(symbol) <= 40 and symbol.endswith("USDT")
            and all(ch.isalnum() for ch in symbol))


def admit_dynamic(symbol: str) -> str:
    candidate = symbol.strip().upper() if isinstance(symbol, str) else ""
    if not _shape_ok(candidate):
        raise SymbolNotSupported(symbol)
    _dynamic.add(candidate)
    return candidate


def retire_dynamic(symbol: str) -> None:
    _dynamic.discard(symbol)


def dynamic_symbols() -> tuple[str, ...]:
    return tuple(sorted(_dynamic))


def is_dynamic(symbol: object) -> bool:
    """Admitted at runtime and not one of the build's own instruments."""
    return isinstance(symbol, str) and symbol in _dynamic and symbol not in SUPPORTED_SYMBOLS


def permitted_symbols() -> tuple[str, ...]:
    """The whitelist, then whatever is admitted at runtime."""
    return SUPPORTED_SYMBOLS + tuple(s for s in sorted(_dynamic) if s not in SUPPORTED_SYMBOLS)


class SymbolNotSupported(ValueError):
    """A symbol outside the whitelist. Raised before anything is read or sent."""

    code = SYMBOL_NOT_SUPPORTED

    def __init__(self, symbol: object) -> None:
        self.symbol = symbol
        super().__init__(
            f"{symbol!r}는 지원 심볼이 아닙니다. "
            f"지원: {', '.join(SUPPORTED_SYMBOLS)}")
        self.message = str(self)


def is_supported(symbol: object) -> bool:
    return isinstance(symbol, str) and (symbol.strip().upper() in SUPPORTED_SYMBOLS
                                        or symbol.strip().upper() in _dynamic)


def resolve(symbol: object | None) -> str:
    """The canonical symbol for a request, or a refusal.

    `None` and the empty string mean "the caller did not choose", which is the default symbol -
    that is what keeps every existing single-symbol caller working unchanged. Anything else is
    normalised (trimmed, upper-cased) and then has to be in the whitelist; a near miss like
    "btcusd" or "BTCUSDT " is accepted or refused on its normalised form, never half-matched.
    """
    if symbol is None:
        return DEFAULT_SYMBOL
    if not isinstance(symbol, str):
        raise SymbolNotSupported(symbol)
    candidate = symbol.strip().upper()
    if not candidate:
        return DEFAULT_SYMBOL
    if candidate not in SUPPORTED_SYMBOLS and candidate not in _dynamic:
        raise SymbolNotSupported(symbol)
    return candidate


def base_asset(symbol: str) -> str:
    """The coin a quantity is denominated in, for a label only.

    Derived by stripping the USDT quote because these three are all USDT-quoted perpetuals, and
    it exists for the one case where a screen needs a unit *before* `exchangeInfo` has been

    return candidate[:-4] if candidate.endswith("USDT") else candidate

unit_text.usb-crypto-paper:
# /etc/systemd/system/usb-crypto-paper.service
[Unit]
Description=US-B CRYPTO Terminal BTCUSDT/ETHUSDT/SOLUSDT (PAPER: Bybit public data, simulated fills | BINANCE LIVE: real USDs-M manual orders, disarmed at boot)
Documentation=file:/root/usb/docs/crypto/CRYPTO_SERVER_RUNBOOK_V1.md
After=network-online.target
Wants=network-online.target

[Service]
Type=simple
User=root
WorkingDirectory=/root/usb_runtime/crypto_paper

# The equity /root/usb/.env is still deliberately NOT loaded. It carries the Kiwoom profile
# and the broker mode, and this app must never be able to read them: the crypto package
# imports nothing from the equity side.
#
# What changed: this service now holds one exchange credential, for Binance USDs-M manual
# trading, scoped to a file of its own inside this service's tree rather than shared with
# the equity side. The boundary that mattered - crypto cannot see the equity broker, and the
# equity services cannot see the Binance key - is preserved by the split, not by absence.
#
# BINANCE_LIVE_TRADING_ENABLED=true in that file is a *capability*: it says this host may
# send an order. It is not an arm. The second gate is an in-memory session that starts
# disarmed on every boot, needs a confirmation phrase typed in the UI, and expires on its
# own - so a restart, a crash or a deploy always comes back unable to trade.
# BINANCE_LIVE_CLIENT_ARMED is deliberately absent from that file; setting it would arm the
# account from boot forever and defeat the whole arrangement.
EnvironmentFile=/root/usb_runtime/crypto_paper/secrets/binance_live.env
Environment=PYTHONPATH=/root/usb_runtime/crypto_paper/src/backend
Environment=PYTHONUNBUFFERED=1
Environment=CRYPTO_PAPER_RUN_CONFIG=/root/usb_runtime/crypto_paper/run/run_config.json
Environment=CRYPTO_PAPER_ROOT=/root/usb_runtime/crypto_paper/run
Environment=CRYPTO_SYMBOL_REFERENCE_ROOT=/root/usb_runtime/crypto_paper/symbols

# --workers 1 is a correctness requirement, not a capacity choice. The paper engine is a single
# in-memory account that appends to one input tape and one ledger. A second worker would hold a
# second account, append interleaved records to the same files, and the next restart would
# replay a tape that never described one run. Recovery would refuse it, or worse, not notice.
# Entrypoint is `terminal.server`, not `terminal.api`: it imports api's app and registers the
# D3.5 sizing route onto that same instance. Pointing systemd at `api:app` would start a
# terminal without /api/crypto/sizing, and the screen's quick-size buttons would go dead.
ExecStart=/root/usb/.venv/bin/uvicorn app.crypto.terminal.server:app \
  --host 127.0.0.1 --port 8100 --workers 1 --no-access-log

Restart=always
RestartSec=5
KillSignal=SIGTERM
TimeoutStopSec=30
MemoryMax=200M
Nice=5

[Install]
WantedBy=multi-user.target

# /etc/systemd/system/usb-crypto-paper.service.d/segment-compression.conf
[Service]
Environment=CRYPTO_PAPER_COMPRESS_SEGMENTS=true

unit_text.usb-grouped-daily.timer:
# /etc/systemd/system/usb-grouped-daily.timer
[Unit]
Description=Collect the grouped daily Strategy A reads as D-1, after Massive publishes it

[Timer]
# Stocks Basic does not publish a session until after midnight ET, which is why the E universe
# build sits at 00:20 ET. Measured, not assumed: the forward store's eleven grouped files were
# each written at 00:20-00:22 ET on the session's next calendar day, seven nights in a row and
# across a weekend. 00:40 ET is twenty minutes behind that build (which completes in ~20s, so
# the shared Massive key is free) and three hours five minutes ahead of the 03:45 ET paper
# start that attaches A. Mon..Fri covers every session: a Friday close is collected on Monday,
# and a holiday Monday collects Friday again as a no-op.
OnCalendar=Mon..Fri 00:40 America/New_York
Persistent=true
AccuracySec=1m
RandomizedDelaySec=0
Unit=usb-grouped-daily.service

[Install]
WantedBy=timers.target
unit_text.usb-h-forward.timer:
# /etc/systemd/system/usb-h-forward.timer
[Unit]
Description=Update the Strategy H-V2 forward shadow once a session, after Massive publishes it

[Timer]
# Measured against the same evidence usb-grouped-daily.timer was set from: a session is published
# after midnight ET on its next calendar day, and the grouped store's files for 2026-10-05..08 were
# each written at 00:40 ET the following morning. 01:10 ET is therefore safely past publication.
#
# It is also where the shared Massive key is idle: usb-e-universe runs 00:20 ET, usb-grouped-daily
# 00:40 ET and usb-splits-refresh 00:55 ET. The Basic plan allows 5 calls per minute across all of
# them and each client paces only itself, so H is placed 15 minutes behind the last of the three
# rather than alongside any of them. It is 2h35m ahead of the 03:45 ET paper start that attaches A.
#
# 01:10 ET is also inside the band where the server's own date (the host runs KST) and the ET
# session date agree - 01:10 ET is 14:10 KST the same day - so the updater's "today" upper bound
# cannot run a day ahead of the sessions it is asking for. No KST hour is written here;
# America/New_York keeps this DST-safe.
#
# Mon..Fri, the same cadence as the grouped-daily source it shadows: a Friday session is collected
# on Monday, and a holiday Monday re-asks for Friday as a no-op. Between Friday's close and Monday
# the store simply carries the gap, which is the honest state - outcomes report PENDING rather than
# maturing against a substituted price. Weekends make no external call at all.
OnCalendar=Mon..Fri 01:10 America/New_York
# A missed run (host down, suspended) fires once on the next boot. Harmless by construction: the
# updater recomputes which sessions are missing from the store, so a late run collects exactly the
# same gaps a punctual one would have.
Persistent=true
AccuracySec=1m
RandomizedDelaySec=0
Unit=usb-h-forward.service

[Install]
WantedBy=timers.target
